## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kakkaṭakajātaka* (Ja 267), translated under the title *The Golden Crab*, is a canonical birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded on SuttaCentral, the tale opens with the reference "Gold-clawed creature" and was recounted by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana near Sāvatthī in relation to a certain woman [SuttaCentral].
In terms of parallels and text reuse, automated analysis by DharmaNexus records no Pali-internal text reuse and no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora reaching the match threshold [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral similarly identifies no curated parallels in other early Buddhist canons, though it documents four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
None of the reference passages retrieved in the research dossier directly discuss Ja 267. The matches generated by automated queries either represent citations of the *Journal Asiatique* (JA 267), typographical misattributions of other stories such as the *Kurudhamma-jātaka* (Ja 276), or narrative mentions of crabs (*kakkaṭaka*) in separate tales including the *Bakajātaka* (Ja 38) and the *Suvaṇṇakakkaṭakajātaka* (Ja 389).
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
